utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we resume the examination of the witness, I'd like to inform the parties that we still have to hear argument on the Prosecution's intention to adduce non-oral testimony, the application of article 92 bis. As we've seen, you've given notice to the Defence, and the Defence has objected. So we'll have to hear the parties on that. I'd rather not do it now right away. As far as I understood, it will take some time before you seek to introduce these statements in evidence. That means that we could use whenever there's a moment where no witnesses are available to be examined, that we then could use that time to have oral argument on these objections raised by the Defence. So I would urge the parties to be at all times prepared for such oral argument. It's just a matter of efficiency that I'm not fixing at this moment a certain date. If of course there will not come a moment in the near future that there are no witnesses, then of course we'll fix a certain moment when we'll hear more about the objections and the reasons why the Prosecution seeks to adduce these non-oral statements in evidence. So be prepared. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the reasons I outlined two days ago, at this stage we only have six witnesses for the four days of hearing next week, and therefore following the calling of those six witnesses may be an opportune time to have those submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. That's what I had in mind as a matter of fact. So the Defence is aware of that as well, and as soon as we run short of witnesses, we'll use the time to have oral argument. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Merely to say that this is a matter of organisation which will be dealt with by your Chamber. But for the next week, at this stage I do not think we are quite organised for that on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Monday to start with. That's fine. Then I think we can continue the cross-examination of Mr. Grabovica. Yes, please, Mr. Usher, would you please bring the witness into the courtroom. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I was just looking at the transcript what I said and it seems that it wasn't quite clear here. That is that I could not be hear at the hearing on Monday. I have already apologised for that, but that is what I just said, I won't be able to be present here on Monday. I'm sorry, but I hope that the Chamber understood what I just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... quite clear. I don't expect that the oral argument will take place on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Grabovica, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Grabovica, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you made yesterday. That may go without saying, but I just remind you. Then, Ms. Pilipovic, you may proceed with the cross-examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, good morning, everybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we adjourned when you answered how many passengers were on the bus. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, at the moment when you heard the shot, what happened then? You said that you had heard the passengers screaming and that you switched on the engine and started?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is quite true that I heard passengers screaming. I stood up from my steering wheel. I could see a woman holding on to her knee on one side of the bus. On the other side of the bus there was another women all covered in blood because she had been hit in an artery and there was a pool of blood underneath her.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A man suggested to block the artery with one's hand. I would have done that same -- I would have done that myself, but I thought it would be best if I went to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you went to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I switched on the engine, closed the doors, and started for the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at the hospital, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The passengers in the bus were still panicking from the doors, there was a sniper on the faculty of theology. I wasn't paying attention to what the passengers were saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that all the passengers were in the bus with you as you went to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, all the passengers were in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And when did the passengers leave the bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I reached the hospital, in front of the hospital, there was some medical personnel who were waiting with stretchers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who it is who had announced your arrival to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know who it was but they knew that somebody was about to arrive.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How long did it take you from the place where the alleged incident happened to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I had to turn the bus and go over the pavement and along and then it didn't take more than two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain how could the medical personnel learn in that interval that you were coming, that is how could they be notified so as to be there waiting for you in front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there was a team which was on duty and waiting there all the time. But when I arrived there, they were waiting in front of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And after the passengers who, as you say, had been injured, you left them in the hospital, after you left them in the hospital what did you as the bus driver do with the bus? What happened next?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the medical personnel and other passengers happened to get those passengers off the bus, and the medical personnel because I presumed that the doctor had said that a woman marked as B had bled a great deal, had lost a lot of blood.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do with the bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went back with the bus to the garage. It is Velikih Drveta on Alipasino Bridge.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you report the incident to the police?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the garage, and the local police came for inspection.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us from what part of the city did the local police come?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly, but they examined the bus. They saw where the bullet penetrated. They took photographs, made the record. And I don't know, I'm not the investigator to know what happened after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make a statement on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did what I'm doing today and here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You are telling us, you mean, that the vehicle, the bus, was photographed and that the hole was inspected, the bullet hole, that it was inspected?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And after that, after the incident and after you gave your statement where you sum it again?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a year later, a man came to my address and asked me to give a statement, asked me if I remembered what it was and how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that those passengers and you called them passengers A and B, do you have any knowledge as to the state of their health later on?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, I learned that person B had succumbed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And if I show you the testimonies, Witness, of persons A and B who were in the bus, will you accept, that both witnesses A and B survived and are living in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, since you told us that the local police had come and performed the investigation, do you have any knowledge if a few days after the incident, the media said that the person who had fired at the bus had been arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the Defence should like to show the statement of the witness who was on the bus. We received the statement from our learned friends. The statement was made on the 30th of August, 2000. It was a person who was in that bus and who was injured in her legs testifying to the fact that I just examined the witness, says something different, says something else. And I have her statement in English. It is page 5 in B/C/S and page 0012-18 in English. I have it in the sufficient number of copies, the statements, can it please be given to the interpreters and the interpreters' booths, and I will read only this part of the statement and I will invite the witness to give us his opinion. That is, 30th of August, 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, we would respectfully request a copy of this statement. We don't seem to have it with us here this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I hear that there are a sufficient number of copies available. So, Mr. Usher, would you please. May I assume, Ms. Pilipovic, that you're going to read a specific part of the statement to the witness? Is it your intention to call this since I do understand that this is someone who has given a statement --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Will they be called by the Prosecution or is it one of the witnesses on the list to be called by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The Defence wishes to propose that the part of the statement on page 5 referring to the person who fired at the bus be introduced as a Defence exhibit because we already heard a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If anyone misses a page, 01039216 which opens with the witness statement, I have a double copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I will read to you the statement of Witness A as you marked her in the bus who was present in the bus, and that is page 5 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters were not given copies of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Page 5 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that the interpreters have not got copies of the statement. Is that true? Or do you just have the English version, Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have it in B/C/S, too, but only one copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please provide it to the interpreters booth to start with so that we can avoid any difficulties in the translation. May I just ask you, Ms. Pilipovic: I have four pages in front of me now, the first one last two digits are 14. The second is with the last two digits 16, and the third 17, the fourth 18. 15 I would expect would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be there as well, but I've got no idea whether it's relevant or not. Yes, I see. That's the reason why I got two 16s. Madam Registrar, would you have another 9215 for me because it was not 17 that was missing but 15 that was missing. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has the page with 15, but there are only signatures on this page. And we have a number of copies, but I -- because I will be reading only the text which is on page 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I will be reading the passage 6. "At the time that I was shot in the bus, I was not aware where had the shots come from. Later on, I was told that a Serb called Goran Vasic was the one who had shot the bus. I saw it on Bosnian television some days later that Vasic had been arrested. The announcer said that his name was Vasic, and that he had been arrested for shooting at the bus. I was also told by my son that a man who had shot the bus had been arrested and that he had admitted that he had shot at the bus. My memory is not entirely clear on this point." Witness, did you understand what I just read?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, completely. May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you first wait what questions will be put to you on this issue, and then if there's any additional thing you would like to tell the Court, you'll -- I'll give you the opportunity for that. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the course of the few days following the incident with the bus that you were driving, did you in the media or perhaps in some other way learn that a person called Goran Vasic had been arrested and that it was he who had fired at the bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that Goran Vasic had been arrested, but I repeat, I do not know who it was that fired the bullet but I know the direction that it came from and it came from Nedzarici, that is from an area which was held by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you know that Goran Vasic was arrested in relation to the incident?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know he was arrested in relation to that incident, but I knew that he was -- I know that he was arrested. It is today that I heard here for the first time that it was Goran Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Since it was on Bosnian television, do you have any knowledge as to who it was who arrested him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, believe me, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn whether it was the, if I may call it that, the Bosnian police who arrested him or the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember in what part of the city was he arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, but I heard that he lived on Kasindolska.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where is that street, in what part of the city? I assume it is Dobrinja, is it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is opposite Nedzarici, in the direction of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that part of the city called anything special?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So we now heard from you that you did know at that time when the incident happened that after a while, a man was arrested under the name of Goran Vasic that had shot at the bus. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time today that I heard that it was Goran Vasic who shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please indicate exactly the source where the witness said that the arrest of Goran Vasic was an arrest of a man that had shot at the bus? Because I heard the witness testify several times that he knew about an arrest, but he did not know that this arrest was in relation with a suspicion that he would have shot at the bus. His testimony I think two, perhaps even three times, I'm not quite sure about that, was quite clear as far as I see. So I would like you to indicate the source exactly where the witness's testimony was to the -- was what you indicated in your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my colleagues will try and check it in the transcript, and if not, I will rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. In fact, I believe that there is a contradiction. We are finding ourselves on page 10, line 3 where the witness said that he heard that Goran Vasic had been arrested, and certainly he said he didn't know whether that was in relation to the shooting of the bus. But I think that he later said he didn't even know the name and that he had only just found out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The contradiction comes out very clearly on page 10, line 3 where the witness said: "I heard that Goran Vasic had been arrested," and then on line 9, he then says that this is the first time that he hears today that it was Goran Vasic who shot the bus. So I believe that this is a contradiction and I'm sure that Ms. Pilipovic will rephrase her question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think there's all reason to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, when you heard that Goran Vasic was arrested, did you know why he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that he was arrested because of what he did in Kasindolska Street, but it is the first time that I hear today that it was him who had shot at the bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So Witness, you will allow for the possibility that the witness who had stated that she heard on Bosnian television that he was arrested because of the shooting on the bus, that you did not hear this?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I listened to the radio a lot, but this is the first time today here that it was Goran Vasic who had shot at the bus. I heard that Goran Vasic was arrested because of what he did in Kasindolska Street because he killed Hakija Turajlic because of the murder of Hakija Turajlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I noticed that the Livenote transcript system seems to have stopped working several questions back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I see the same. I was looking on my -- on the big screen and not on my laptop screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. President, someone is on their way to fix it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it -- you don't have Livenote on the -- well, it doesn't move any more. Let's just wait and see what the technicians can do for us. Perhaps we could use the time, Madam Registrar, to complete the rather confusing copies of the statement. Would you have another page with last two digits 15 and 1-7?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please take care of the distribution of ... I'm still confident that by the end of the trial, we will be able to be organised in the sense that a few copies of five pages could be distributed without any double pages or missing pages. I'm still confident.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to use this time while we're distributing the pages just to say that the Defence doesn't always have the automatic distribution of copies, and this is why we sometimes have problems. But we also hope that by the end of the trial, everything will be going much more smoothly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see that the Livenote is functioning again. We all have received the papers now in the order as we learned them to put in kindergarten, and let's now proceed. There is a problem in the Livenote, as I see it on page 12, line 10. The question to the witness was "Witness, when you heard that Goran Vasic was arrested, did you know why he was arrested?" And then the answer was, "I heard he was arrested because of what he did in Kasindolska Street" although it does not appear, the name of the street, in Livenote, "it is the first time I hear today that it was him who had shot at the bus." Ms. Pilipovic, that is where the Livenote ends, so I'd like to invite you to resume your questioning at that very moment since I remember, which is not in the Livenote, that the witness testified later on that it was because of a murder that Mr. Vasic was arrested. So that as a whole is not appearing in the Livenote. So would you then please resume at that very moment when you asked him about the arrest of Mr. Vasic. I'm sorry for the technical problems, but we are on our feet again. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us, when you heard that Goran Vasic was arrested, did you find out that he had been arrested because he had shot at the bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm repeating again. This is the first time that I hear today that Goran Vasic was the one who had shot at the bus. I heard that Goran Vasic was arrested because of the deed he did in Kasindolska Street because the murder of Hakija Turajlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you're telling us that on Bosnian television, you did not hear that Goran Vasic was arrested because of the shooting at the bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Yesterday, while you were examined by my learned colleague, on page 76, line 6, it was 13.06 -- 13.16, you said it wasn't military police in question but civilian police.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you telling us that you can make -- you can tell them apart, the military police and the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell them apart.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police was not around there, and I wouldn't even know what they look like. Sometimes when I was a soldier I used to see them in the barracks when I was a soldier of the JNA. But the local police would wear just side arms, and you could see them everywhere, in peacetime as well, and here today.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of the fact that how the civilian police was dressed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot quite remember. I believe they were perhaps green uniforms. There were all kinds of uniforms, a little mix. They didn't have real uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You say that they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably officially issued weapons. Every policeman had official weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in 1992, 1993, or 1994 in Sarajevo, civilian police, as you say, were on the front lines, were present on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness photograph C, and this is 4296 Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you put on the ELMO photograph C, which number ends with 4296.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you photograph marked C. Could you look at this photograph and tell us about this part which is marked in red. Yesterday, I understood that you said that this is where the barricades were.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what these barricades were made from?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were anti-sniping barricades, and they were made of old tin sheeting, old buses, old lorries. There were some blankets there as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What was the height of the barricades?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The height of the barricades was about 3 to 4 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Before the moment -- the incident in question, how often did you come to this intersection at your starting bus stop?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never came before the war, when I was driving a trolley bus. This is where the trolley bus used to drive. And then during the war -- before the war, I never came there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on this photograph in this part that -- where you had marked the circle and the barricades, in relation to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. barricades, how far away from there was the front line? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because of these buildings how far exactly the front lines were. This is Dobrinja II, so it would then be adjoining the Nedzarici. I don't know how far the front line of the BH army was, but I am certain it went on into -- this was adjoining the Nedzarici settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that the bullet had come from the direction of these two houses that we can see?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether a part of Nedzarici with such small houses were under the control of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe perhaps these first houses, but these two houses I don't know. I don't know whether they were there. I don't know where the lines were.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said the bullet had come -- the shot had come from the faculty of theology.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us on what basis do you claim that the bullet had come from there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the intersection where I was standing, you can see the faculty of theology.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how far in relation to the intersection is the faculty of theology from that place?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I cannot give you an estimate. But perhaps 600, 700 metres approximately.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the hills that we can see on the photograph behind these lower houses, or what are these hills? Can you tell us that? Is that a part of a mountain or a hill? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite far. That's outside of Sarajevo. I cannot recognise it. From Nedzarici, there's no mountain so you can see quite far away in this part.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell us about the intersection where you were turning your bus as your terminus and your first stop, what are the streets that cross there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction I came from, on one side is the street of Omladinskih Brigada, and the on the other side is the street of Nikole Demonje. The street where the bullet had come from, just give me a moment, it was before called avenue, avena of something. It used to have a different name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you this is now the Bulevar of the Defenders of Dobrinja, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness a map, a part of a map of town of the Dobrinja area so that he can mark on the map exactly where the stop was as well as where the faculty of theology was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. Mr. Usher, could you assist Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Usher, since the witness is asked to do some markings, would you please put the map on the ELMO, return the photo to Madam Registrar. Yes, perhaps you could turn the ELMO in such a way that the witness can do whatever marking is necessary from where he sits. And would you please provide him with a black marker. And could we please zoom in a bit on the ELMO because ... Would you please put it a bit higher, Mr. Usher. A bit to the left. Yes. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you identify for us on this map which part of town we have here?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in this part where it says Nedzarici, could you identify for us the place that you say was the faculty of theology?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It isn't very clear, but I will do my best.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like you to take a black marker pen, and if you can mark that place, circle it, and put number "1" where the faculty of theology is.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see. Can I use this map?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Witness. I gave you that map to circle and tell us where the place is. As soon as you mark it, could you please put it on the ELMO so we can all see?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please put the map on the ELMO so we can see on our screen Mr. Grabovica what you're doing. So the map is now on the ELMO, the machine to your right-hand side. Just forget about your screen in front of you and concentrate on the map as it is to your right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you've just circled.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first place that I circled was the place where I had stopped with the bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please put number "1" next to it.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And the second place you circled is the faculty of theology. Put number "2."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in relation to place number 1, looking at place number 2, what is -- what kind of buildings are there that are towards the faculty of theology?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are private houses that are a bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the place that you marked number 1 and where you've circled, what part of Dobrinja is this?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the centre of Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Looking towards the faculty of theology, which parts of the Dobrinja we can see before you get to Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dobrinja II, and Dobrinja III.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark on the map, looking towards place number 1 and place number 2, could you mark where Dobrinja II is and where Dobrinja III is.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I will mark with numbers "2" and "3."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a bit confusing as a matter of fact. Would you please do them as number "2" with an asterisk and number "3" with an asterisk otherwise we have two numbers "2" on the map. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So for the transcript, numbers 2 and 3 with asterisk, the witness marked Dobrinja II and Dobrinja III. As far as we can see on this map, in relation to the faculty of theology, from point 1 to point 2, we can see the Dobrinja II and Dobrinja III settlements. Could you tell us the type of buildings which existed in Dobrinja II and Dobrinja III? Are these apartment blocks or are these family houses?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On both sides, there are apartment blocks. And between Dobrinja II and Dobrinja III is former street called Avenue, and this is the direction between these two series of apartment blocks which is not covered by any kinds of houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Witness, and mark for us on this map with a black line where, according to you, the settlement of Nedzarici begins with family houses, private houses?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can try. I will put a straight line.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of the street, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure what the name of the street is, but further down is former Branislava Nusica Street, Bore Draskovica Street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. You told us that in 1992, on the 15th of April, you stopped driving a trolley bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From then on, until the moment that you started to drive again in 1994, when you started to drive a bus this time, were you still employed at your company?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So the period from 1992 until 1994 you did not work?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, did you have a work obligation regardless of the fact that the company wasn't working?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a work obligation, and I was also a military conscript.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So in that period from 1992 to 1994, you were a soldier?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the logistics.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us which unit this was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was a -- some kind of 105th.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Was this 105th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us this 105th Motorised Brigade, was it based in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Where was the headquarters of the 105th Motorised Brigade, in which part of the town?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope you'll believe me when I say I do not know where that was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And whilst you were a member of the 105th Motorised Brigade, were you ever on the front line?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how much time did you spend in your unit?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day, and then I would have two days off.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that one day when you were, to put it that way, in your unit, does that mean the whole day and the whole night?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where did other members of your unit sleep at the time when they were on the front lines?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would spend a day and a night at the front line, and then they would be sleeping two days and two nights.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what parts of the city were the front lines of the 105th Motorised?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Gromolj in the lower part of Poljine.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which municipality is that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we could not hear the witness's answer because the day of the counsel and of the witness overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could I ask you not to answer the question when the screen is still moving because the interpreters first have to translate. And if you immediately answer, they cannot do it. Could you please repeat the answer, and if necessary, Ms. Pilipovic will put the question to you again, to the last question.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the last question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long was the front line in the part of the city where the 105th Motorised Brigade was deployed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Localities of Gromolj, Glave, Brekin Potok.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And whilst you were with the 105th Motorised Brigade, where did the other members of the brigade sleep?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They slept at home.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many -- how strong was the 105th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you were promoted or did you acquire a rank whilst you were a member of the 105th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I just consult with my colleague, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you were in the logistics. Can you tell us where did you come for work? I suppose you had a workplace somewhere. Can you tell us what street and what building?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The street, Saburina Street in the elementary school. That is where the logistics of the 105th Motorised Brigade was housed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How many of you were in that elementary school?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were about 50 there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what did you wear?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us when you went to work, what did you wear and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. did you have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was in civilian clothes, never put on a uniform. I never had a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: One more question: Can you answer me, did you have some ID or something else to tell you apart, which you could show that -- to prove that you were a member of the 105th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, we had the Territorial Defence, so that we had the TO IDs.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later on, units were formed, and I was assigned to a labour duty, rather than to a workplace that I had before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has no more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just a couple of brief questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Grabovica, I believe yesterday, as reflected in the Livenote transcript, page 75, lines 3 and 4, you stated that all the passengers on the bus were women. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do remember it. For the most part it was women. There could have been a man, perhaps two, but for the most part it was women.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grabovica. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has one or more additional questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Witness, I believe I heard you say, and I will quote in English, [In English] ... "Was to drive civilians only." [Interpretation] Could you deny the military to board the bus?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not deny admission to anyone, but the military did not use the buses. If there were any men on those buses, they would be in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You said also, and I quote: [In English] "Was the military police, or rather the local civilian police." [No Interpretation] [In English] "Military police and local civilian police"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose that there is a difference, but I never came across the military police. I only came across civilian police, those same -- the same police that I come across today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Has there ever been an exchange of fire between the police near the bus stop and the police -- and the snipers in other parts?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there, when I was there, when I drove my bus there, I never saw any such exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, please, my last question has to do with the bus coming to the stop. I believe you marked in the videocassette that the bus has passed and stopped after the pedestrian crossing. And on the photograph, it seemed to me that the stop is before the crossing. And I'll explain it if you like. On the videotape, you marked the front part of the bus which has passed, or rather which was at the intersection. On the photograph, it is slightly at the back. Is that indeed the exact spot where the stop, or rather is it the photograph which is correct or is it the tape which is correct because they are marked slightly differently?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a turn at that intersection to go back to the terminal. That is, at this intersection, I had to make a U-turn, and I was standing where I pointed. And this is where the bus was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But it is beyond the place marked on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus -- more than half of the bus was at the intersection, that is, the bus was -- the bigger part of the bus was in the intersection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the bus stops?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were no regular bus stops. Wherever there were groups of people who were waiting, we would stop. And people stopped to wait for the bus at different places that were shielded. We did not have any regular bus stops because of security reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Grabovica, also one question for you: As far as I understand, in your first statement given to the investigators of the Prosecutor's Office, you mentioned the day of the 17th of May. Then in your second statement, if I do understand it well, you mentioned the month of May. And during testimony in this Court, you said it was the 25th of May that the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did anyone help you in refreshing your recollection as far as the 25th of May is concerned? Have there been any suggestions or did someone help you in refreshing your memory as far as the date is concerned prior to giving testimony in this court?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us how you were helped to find the day of the 25th of May which was part of your testimony in this Court?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When your investigators asked me about the registration plates, I said they were the old ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what is the relation between old registration plates and exactly the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to my company to check about the plates, and they told me that the incident had happened on the 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they explain to you how they could locate this incident in time exactly on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my company, they keep records about the bus. There's the travel order and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I do understand you well that it's on the basis of the records in your company of which the information has been given to you at your request that you testify that it was on the 25th of May?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ GRABOVICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your clear answer in this respect. Mr. Grabovica, you've answered all the questions put to you by both the parties and by the Chamber. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague, which is quite a journey, as we all are aware of. You also understand that it is very important for this Court to hear the answers to the questions put by parties and by the Chamber itself since we need these answers to prepare the decisions we'll have to make. Coming to The Hague means assisting the Court in performing this task. Thank you very much for having come to The Hague, and I wish you a safe journey home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. If necessary, if there are more questions, I am quite willing to answer them. I saw quite a great deal. There were many other incidents on the buses. I can testify about all that I saw and all that I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can imagine. You have been called by the Prosecution. The Prosecution has asked you the questions they wanted to ask you, and I can imagine that you could tell us a lot more about what happened in these years. But we leave it to the parties to find out what questions they would put to you. And you'll be aware that there are a lot of other witnesses who will testify on other events that happened in those years. So thank you very much. Mr. Usher, could you please lead the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we still have to decide upon the admission into evidence. Let's first start with the Prosecution documents. As far as I can see, we started with the video being shown to the witness. Madam Registrar, would you have a P number for that? I see apart from the usual objections, we'll admit it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The video that was shown yesterday by the Prosecution is P3280M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the next is the 360 degree photograph on the CD Rom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That exhibit is P3279M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we have a set of three photos.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The set of three photos are P3274A, B, and C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think these are the -- are there any difficulties? I think we usually, if it's in the transcript, if a series of photos has got one number as it is now, we usually only give this one number. But it's clear from the transcript that this number covers three photos.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the Defence conferring but doesn't result in any ... Then, I think these were the Prosecution documents. And then we have the Defence tendered the statement of a witness. I see the Prosecution is conferring. Will this result in ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prosecution has no objections to that document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Bench, however, has some problems with it. And I can tell you why. Our usual procedure is that we read part of the previous statements. A specific part has been read to the witness. The last line was of this statement on this issue: "My memory is not entirely clear on this point." The witness has been confronted with this part of the statement. None of the other parts of the statement have been part of the testimony. So I think, according to our usual procedure, everything the witness is confronted with is in the transcript, has been read to it. And I do not see at this moment that there's any real contradiction apart from that the person who gave the previous statement has seen something on television which the witness has said he has not seen on television and gives a different reason for the arrest of a certain Mr. Vasic. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. The specific reason for which the Defence believes that this document should be admitted into its entirety, as a whole, is as follows: The witness stated that the woman called B succumbed to the injuries received in that attack, if I remember him well, one day later or shortly afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness had not testified that the lady was dead. The witness has testified that he heard the next day that the lady succumbed, as it is in the English translation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Therefore, this witness said that woman B had succumbed to the wounds one or two days later, and it is important for the credibility to show that this same person B was obviously alive and perfectly healthy because she could testify before the -- and sign her statement with her own hand. And therefore, the statement has a date and admitted so that it could be examined so that one could check the credibility of the witness whom we have just heard because obviously one -- one who has succumbed cannot sign such a statement as this witness did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please give me time to think, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I merely wanted to say for the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll just read again the transcript. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is for the transcript, what I just said was succubus and not succumbed. There is a very slight difference between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Maybe I could read the line 15, page 6. The answer was: "The next day, I learned that person B had succumbed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you think it's to be necessary to tender this whole statement as evidence that Mrs. B, although I do not for sure know that it's the same, but it's very likely that it's the same person. I didn't hear any questions asked about it. Let's just assume, then, that Mrs. B was one of the passengers in the bus, is there any misunderstanding between the parties that Mrs. B did not die from this incident? As far as I can provisionally assess the evidence given before, where it is in evidence that the passengers who were injured during this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. incident left hospital after ten days of treatment. Is there any -- is it the Prosecution's case that Mrs. B died?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. And in fact, the wording of the schedule in the indictment makes it clear that the woman was allegedly wounded and not killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So for the establishment of the fact that Mrs. B died, there is no necessity whatsoever to admit this document into evidence. As far as the reliability of the witness statement is concerned, I do not see whether the mere testimony that Mr. Grabovica was told that Mrs. B died would make it unreliable. It is in no saying that he could have been told something which did not happen, and it's among the parties; there's no dispute about whether Mrs. B was alive. So for that reason, there is no reason to admit this document into evidence. And there's another reason which would oppose against admitting it into evidence, because it would admit into evidence a lot of statements which have not been the subject of the examination in this Court. We would have to read all the statement. Whatever questions may come up as far as the other parts of the statements are concerned, because if we admit it into evidence, well, we would have it, we would look at it. While the relevant part has been read literally to the witness. So for these reasons we will not admit the document into evidence. Yes, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having conferred, we believe that it would be quite convenient, and we thank the Chamber for the decision it has taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So then we have only as a remaining document tendered by the Defence the map which has been marked by the witness during his testimony. And that would be, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next number for the Defence's exhibit would be D46.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's D46. May I ask the Defence next time if they give a map to a witness, to use a copy without any markings on it. Because as you'll see, there are some markings already on this map. And it's unintended, of course. If there's an intended -- I see some circles around, or you gave us another one. I'll tell you exactly where they were. You'll see that around Stup -- you'll see that about around the PTT building, there's a circle. So whenever you have a ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is a very faint trace, Mr. President. I did not see it. You have a better sight obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... done by mistake. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, I did not see it at all. If we can find another map during the interval, then we shall copy it. Otherwise, we'll have to use it. But this is a poor copy. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm quite convinced of your intention to not create any confusion. We'll adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think it's up to the Prosecution to call its next witness, which will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Faruk Kadric, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please, Mr. Usher, would you bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, at the beginning of your testimony, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher, and I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Kadric. Please be seated. Mr. Kadric, you have been called as a witness by the Prosecution. That means that you'll first be examined by Mr. Ierace, counsel for the Prosecution. Then you'll be examined by counsel for the Defence; and if there are any additional questions, the Bench will put them to you as well. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, is your name Faruk Kadric?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you born on the 22nd of February, 1977?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is your birthdate?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: 22 of October, 1977.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the name of your father?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Fajko.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In 1992, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you continue to live in Sarajevo throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In 1993, were you going to school?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During 1993, was there an incident when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the date when that happened?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was on the 4th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to your birthdate, were you aged 15 on that date?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you with anyone when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I was with my father.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were you and your father doing?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: We were in a car. We were driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was it?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It is a vehicle that is used to transport meat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How big was the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: About 2 tonnes. It can carry about 2 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: According to the transcript in English, a little while ago you said we were in a car. Were you in a car?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: In the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Could you please describe the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: The vehicle is intended to transport meat, because we were in a meat processing. And it has three seats. I don't know what else to say about the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What size was the vehicle in terms of tonnes?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: You mean the weight, the weight of the vehicle or just its carrying capacity?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, the weight.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In terms of its carrying capacity, what was its weight?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I think about 2 or 3 tonnes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You said that it had three seats. Were the three seats alongside each other or were some in the front and some in the back?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, it was one next to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was behind the three seats?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: A cabin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were the seats -- all right. Was there any writing on the side of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it said Mesnica, butchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you understand the word "truck"?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it a truck or a car?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: A truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were with your father in that vehicle. Was the vehicle transporting anything at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Flour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And whereabouts were you at the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: We were at the intersection of the 10th Transversal, and the Aleja Branka Bujica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what part of Sarajevo was that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you going to?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: We were taking the flour to the local commune, to the Civilian Protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is the nature of the intersection where you were shot? Is it a T-intersection or a cross intersection?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. As you approached the intersection, did you notice if there were any people around?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: There were no people around. There was an UNPROFOR APC which was located on my right side. But it wasn't quite at the intersection. It was a little further away from the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the APC have any markings on it to indicate that it was UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It said "UNPROFOR" in large black letters, it said "UN".

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that there were three seats. And those seats were in a row. Were you sitting next to the passenger window or in the middle seat?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I was sitting by the right window. The middle seat was empty; and on the left-hand side seat was my father who was driving the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What happened as you crossed the intersection?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I heard a shot. And after that, I only remember that I fell on this middle seat which was on my left side. After that, what I can remember is a soldier, a UN soldier, who was taking a cap off his head, and he put it here on my wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you point to where your wound was, please.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, Mr. President, the witness indicates the right side of his neck. Do you remember whether the passenger window, that is the window immediately on your right, was up or down or somewhere in between?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that you heard a shot.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From what direction did you hear the shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I heard the shot coming from the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. After you received some assistance from the UN soldier, what is the next thing that you remember?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I remember when I was taken out of the APC, because where the hospital -- where the UNPROFOR hospital was, there was some lights that you could not see from the outside because of their reflection. I could only see that I was being taken on a stretcher, and I don't remember anything further.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Following the injury, did you receive treatment for a period of time in a Sarajevo hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which hospital?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was the traumatology clinic, the neurosurgery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What period of time did you stay in hospital in Sarajevo, approximately?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: About a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you receive any further medical treatment after you were discharged from hospital in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: At that time, I did not. But there was a proposal that I should go and have the operation abroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you travel abroad for medical purposes related to your injury?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I went to the United Arab Emirates. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For what period of time did you receive medical treatment in the United Arab Emirates?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: About 19 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask, Mr. President, the witness be shown Exhibit P1781.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is a medical record which has attached to it an English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Letter of discharge from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it relate to you and this injury?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the bottom half of the page, I think there is a section which is titled "case history." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think the second sentence reads: "He was wounded on 4 October, 1993 by a fragmentation bullet in the neck." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that indeed the date that you were injured?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It refers to a fragmentation bullet. Was there one part of a bullet in your body or more than one part?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: More than one part.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be show Exhibit P1701, which comprises three colour photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher, would you assist Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the three photographs in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are they indeed three x-rays?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are they of you?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In what country were they taken, in what state?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: In the United Arab Emirates.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do the x-rays bear a date on which they were taken?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What is that date?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: 16th of October, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that date appear in the bottom -- I'll withdraw that. Could you please place the first of those photographs on the machine to your right with the assistance of the court usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please use the middle pointer and point to that part of the x-ray which contains the date. Point to the actual photograph to your right, not on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please turn the ELMO a bit so that the witness ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the photograph can be moved slightly up the ELMO so we that can see the relevant part. Could the photograph be moved further up the machine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you point to the date again, please.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And indeed. Does the date appear back to front?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, coming back to the time that you were shot, what time of day was it when it happened?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was between 11.00 and 11.30. More precisely, quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that time?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was -- the weather was good. It was fine weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What clothes were you wearing?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I had trousers and a T-shirt. Not a T-shirt, but a sweat shirt, a long-sleeved shirt as I have now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown a map. Mr. President, I propose to give the witness a copy of the map which is P3644, the one that I have here, to be given to him. It's therefore marked P3644.FK. I also have copies for the Bench and my learned colleagues. Three for the Bench and two for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you certainly are aware that FK, if we look at the list of witnesses, might be a similar one. I don't know whether you intend to tender perhaps with the next witness as well a similar map, and then FK would not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate Your Honour's point, Mr. President. Perhaps it should have a different notation. FK1, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: FK1.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's for the witness. Thank you. Please, I would be grateful it the witness could have the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But before I ask you questions about the map, I will ask you some more questions about the x-rays. Could you please look at the x-ray that is on the ELMO, that is the photograph to your right. What part of your body appears in that x-ray?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: My neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the x-ray one sees three or four pieces which are irregularly shaped and which appear in a light blue colour. As a result of conversations with your doctors, do you know what they are?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: These are parts of the fragmentation bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are any parts of the bullet still in your neck?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: All of these fragments that you can see on the x-ray are still lodged in my neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Have your doctors given you an explanation as to why they have not been removed?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Because they can't take it out, because through the neck, all of these nerves go through the neck. And there is a possibility if I had surgery that I would end up paralyzed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, could the second photograph now be placed on the ELMO. For the benefit of the transcript, that's an x-ray which appears to show a mouth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you understand it, is that also an x-ray of you, in particular showing your jaw area and neck?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think on the right side of the x-ray, in the vicinity of the vertebrae, we see four irregular shaped items in a similar pattern to what appears in the first x-ray. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
