utterances.text: All right. And are there any other fragment parts which appear in that x-ray, to your knowledge, as a result of talking with your doctors?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Can you please point to the other fragments.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, Mr. President, the witness points to some objects which appear beneath the -- in the lower jaw beneath the teeth, which is slightly to the right of centre of the x-ray. Perhaps the third x-ray could now be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As a result of conversations with your doctors, do you understand the third x-ray to also depict your neck?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it also show the fragments which remain in that part of your body?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could you please now look at the map which is to your left. Would you open it up and firstly tell us if you recognise it as being a map of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That is a map of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If you are able to, would you find the place where you were shot, and then place that part of the map with the assistance of the usher on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please take a blue marker pen and place a cross on the position where you were shot.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you now please place an arrow indicating the direction in which you were travelling at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any barricades on that intersection?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, but a very small one. It was just a container, a container like those that are mounted on a -- on delivery vans. Could have been about 5 metres long, and it was put there that day. Before that, there were no barricades there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Because we used to use the same street before, and I -- prior to that, I never noticed that barricade there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether other civilians had been shot in that area, that is, the area of the intersection?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know whether any civilians were shot at that intersection either shortly before or after you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: What I know is that same day, a woman was hit there, before I was, and that was early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How did you come to know that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: My mother's fellow worker who works in a bakery called this morning and said that I shouldn't go to school because her fellow worker had been killed that very morning at that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you had gone to school that day, would you have had to pass that same intersection?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, I would have -- yes, I could take this intersection, and there was also another route which I could have used. But it was also exposed to sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That concludes evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I apologise. For the assistance of the Trial Chamber, if it's not already apparently, I should indicate that this evidence relates to scheduled sniping incident number 13. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Defence is ready, and we have already understood it was incident number 13. And on the of that, we shall be asking you the following questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Thank you for coming here. Just a moment ago, you said at the beginning of your examination that you were 15 at the time of the accident. And wouldn't it be as a matter of fact exact to say that you were practically 16?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I was 15. I was to turn 16 on the 22nd of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, I was asking you, thank you very much for the interpretation. Yes, I asked you that because we have two dates of your birth, and you were born indeed in October 1977. Is that it, the 22nd of October? Is that your correct date of birth?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. Witness, at that time, what was the profession of your father?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: He was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: He was a self-employed driver?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I understand that you don't understand. Did your father -- was your father self-employed? Was he in the private sector at the time?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: You mean when that happened or before that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am saying at the time.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: He was working for the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And therefore, who was his employer? Was it the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And what -- Witness, what do you mean by Civil Defence? What is that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: At that time, the Civil Defence took care of people because in the beginning, we had very small stock, so that people were paying for some flour. And that day, we had gone to bring some flour to the Civil Defence for which people had paid in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, those who had paid for it in advance, who was that?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you do not know what was your point of destination, point of delivery that day?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I know very well where we were going, but I do not who it was to be delivered to. I don't know the names of people. I know that people would come to get this flour, to take it away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So, Witness, where were you going? May I ask you that.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: We were going to the place where the Civil Defence was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the Civil Defence, this is the Civil Defence, is it part of the army?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you said the Civil Defence is not the army; your father was not employed by the army?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I asked you this question very clearly. You understood it very well. Will you please look up an exhibit which was already shown you, and this is 5 -- 1701, and one for the original language, and this is the Serbian language. I believe 1781, and may it be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, it is very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you a document, and I believe you have a document in the language which you manage to read. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Witness, you just told me that your father was not a member of the army. Will you then please read in your language, and the interpreters will interpret, what it says in the box. And I hope I will be able to find it to show it, in the box which refers to the insurance and the organisation, the insurance organisation. It is -- just a moment. It is 1781, Exhibit 1781, and it is the seventh box on the left-hand side of the document. Will you tell us, Witness, what you see there?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 5th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Then, Witness, can you explain it to me why, if your father was not, as you told us, in the army, why was his insurance paid, why was the 5th Motorised Brigade of the BH army responsible for his insurance?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Sir, I have to ask you this: We were talking about what happened to me. You did not ask me if my father was in the army or not. You were talking about my wounding that day, what he was doing that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, if a question is put to you, you told this Court that your father was in the Civil Defence, not being a part of the army. The Defence is entitled to ask you any questions about that. Just answer them. There's no need of opposing against the question. You just answer it. And the question was whether you have an explanation for the fact that although you said your father was not a member of the army, on this document it is stated that the work organisation of the holder of the insurance was the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 5th Motorised Brigade. So if you have an explanation for that, give it. If you don't know, tell us. Please answer the question of Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I heard that you didn't know, and I do not know whether that means that you don't have an answer or that you do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, don't you know or don't you have an explanation for that or don't you want to tell us the explanation? What was your answer exactly?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I do not know where this here came from. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that means that you have no explanation for this? Is that right, my understanding?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, Witness. Before you came to the courtroom, you saw this document which came from the clinical centre in Sarajevo, from the Sarajevo university?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you didn't -- didn't you ever object to this fact that the BH army, or more specifically, the 5th Motorised Brigade was mentioned here as the organisation providing the insurance?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is, since it is indicated on this document that the holder of the insurance belonged to the organisation the BH army 5th Motorised Brigade, whether you ever protested at whatever place against this entry in this form.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I see that the Chamber is asking questions which are much clearer than mine. But I will try to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, have then said when you read this document and in the absence of your objection, doesn't it mean that at the time of the incident, your father was a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarity of your answer. Witness, shouldn't you also admit that at the time of the incident, your father was about to deliver certain produce for the army, or more specifically, perhaps for the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't about to deliver this produce for the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And he was to deliver it to the Territorial Defence. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: He was delivering --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Will you please repeat your answer for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, he was taking this produce to the Civil Defence in his own vehicle, that is, that truck was private property. It did not serve the Civil Defence or the army or anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. At that time of the incident which we are placing in October 1993, can I then deduce from your answer that at the same time there were parallelly two organisations, the army on one hand and the Civil Defence on the other. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you know concretely where was the Civil Defence that your father was to deliver goods, where was its seat?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was the property of the heating station in Sarajevo, the heating plant in Sarajevo, and the Civil Defence was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you give us the address, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, was that the first time that you were delivering products to the Civil Defence?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: You mean that day or --?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That day or any other day.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: That day, we had already made two deliveries of flour, and I believe it was the third one that we were doing. I think it was the third one when we were hit by the sniper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I just remind you, you're not speaking the same language as the witness, but I must assume that you're listening to his answer in the original language, since you are putting already the next question to him when the translation in French which I follow now and then is not ready yet. Could you also please pause until we also know the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I will bear in mind. I'm trying to be as fast as my colleague, but nevertheless, thank you very much for your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will show you a map now. And no doubt, you will be able to point at the place, at the site where the incident took place. However, do you know if the building or the seat of the Civil Defence, was it guarded? Was it under guard, I mean by the military?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say no, does it mean that you do not know or that there were no army guards there?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, they were not guarded by the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you -- do you have or did you at the time have friends who were bearing weapons, that is, who were members of some military units?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like the witness to be shown the map which was used in the previous testimony. I have a few copies here. And we can perhaps establish this. However, on this map we have still -- we agree. Yes, we agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much indeed. Mr. Usher, can you please ... I'm drawing to the attention of the Chamber that it is the same document that you received a moment ago, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have before you a section of the map. Do you recognise it as a section of the map of the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to help us to follow it clearly, will you simply point, where is the intersection where you say you were hit? Merely point at it.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness is indicating an intersection which to the left of it is written Studentski Dom. The intersection is where the letter "M" approximately is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I'd like to do, Mr. President, is to ask the witness now to mark that intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Will you please take the black marker. And put a visible cross to mark the place where you sustained your injuries.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Will you now point at the place that you were facing, that is, the area which is indicated here and says Nedzarici. Will you please point at it. Do not mark anything, just point at Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Will you please do it once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Usher, can you please move the map slightly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, will you now, Witness, circle Nedzarici as it appears on this map using the black marker.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, do you want only the name or the area?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I meant the area. I see that the witness has understood because he had done it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, now I'm still referring you to the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, is there a problem here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You concluded, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that he circled the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- be good as understood as just circling around the name. Mr. Kadric, Mr. Piletta-Zanin has asked you to put a circle around Nedzarici. This circle you put, is that the area of Nedzarici or did you just put a circle around the name? Is the area wider or smaller? Could you please first tell us, and then if the area is wider, then perhaps put a circle around the whole area.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, only the name of Nedzarici is circled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then please circle what you would Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. understand to be the area of Nedzarici, say the whole area which you would understand still to belong to what you call Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Do I have to do it absolutely precisely accurately, or can I just do it approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As good as you can, but if you say it might not be precise as to every single street, then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. We think of Nedzarici as being a wider territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Wider than what is on the map or what you just indicated or even wider than you indicated?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Larger than what I have marked. In this direction here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I do of course not exactly know what's the aim of your questioning. Would this do? Do I understand, Mr. Kadric, that at least what you've marked is all what you would call Nedzarici, but even more?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: What I have marked we call it all Nedzarici. That means from this main -- from the tram stop, that is, from the Bulevar Mese Selimovica and then all the way here, we call it Nedzarici. But there are also parts which are it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which are?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: There are parts that are called Tosavjljaci, and other areas, other areas like the people bearing that family name used to live there, and that's what it was called. But in fact all this area is Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would that do? At least we know this is at least, if not more, Nedzarici. Would that be sufficient, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. This is one way to view Nedzarici. One version of Nedzarici. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this absolutely precise exercise. Now, could you tell me where you were living at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So for the transcript, the witness is indicating, and perhaps you could tell me when, that the street ends with the number I believe 389, and this street is located in the enclave which he has just marked which is in Nedzarici. Now, Witness, thank you for your answer. Now, other questions in relation to your vehicle: Do you know if on one or more occasions the vehicle that your father was using had also been used by the army?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "no" does it mean that you don't know or that it was not used?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: This vehicle was not used by the army. This vehicle was only destined for this purpose, and this is only -- we had a load of 2 tonnes and it was used to go to the brewery, and this was only for civilian purposes that this vehicle was ever used. It would go to the brewery and had a 2 tonne cistern installed in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't know the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that last question was not interpreted. I'd be grateful if my friend could repeat the question so that I could know what he asked. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you referred to the destination of Vojnicko Polje. Does this mean a battlefield?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No. This is a settlement which is called Vojnicko Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm taking that into account. Thank you, sir. Witness, since we now know that your father was active in the army in the 5th Brigade, do you know where the premises, where he was exercising his military duty?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, your father never told you where he was when he went to do his duty?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: He never went.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And you yourself, you [Realtime transcript read in error "he"] never knew where the premises of the 5th Brigade were?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No. We couldn't -- we couldn't get out, couldn't get out of our building. How could I know where the brigade was?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The question which begins on line 12 of page 24 reads in English: And you yourself, he never knew where the premises of the 5th Brigade were" I think the interpretation I heard was "you never knew where the premises were." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's how I understood it at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. This is what I believe I had said, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think there's no misunderstanding that was intended. Let me just see whether the question has already been answered. Yes, the question has been answered. The witness says: "How could I know where the brigade was?" So that implies that he didn't know. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes I noticed that, Mr. President. Thank you for your help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you told us about the barricades. Could you indicate on the map that you have on your right where the front lines, confrontation lines between the two parties were?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I propose that you indicated on the map perhaps with an interrupted line so that we could then refer to it afterwards. Is that all right if we use the black, since the Chamber is using the red, and I believe the red and the black will go excellently together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please use the black marker, then, and then indicate the front line as you just indicated it on the map with a dotted line.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, for the transcript, the witness has just marked an area which is on the inside as being Nedzarici, but on the -- slightly on the right side of that area. Now, Witness, in this area, were you able to see, since you told us that you lived in the centre of that area, were you able to see these front lines?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you lived in the area, and you never saw the lines. Is that how I should understand it?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, I did not see it because I never went out anywhere. I did not have an opportunity to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, you told us you were not going out, but I believe that you did go out in any case three times for the deliveries in the truck. Now, could you indicate on the map the route that you took? In any case, the two rounds of deliveries that you took before the third when the incident happened. What was the route that you took for the deliveries?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you think you could do it a little more slowly so that we can all see, please?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you very much. And I will ask you, perhaps, to use the red, if that is all right with the Chamber, so it can be more easily -- or perhaps we can use a different type of line so that we can tell apart the lines, what does the Chamber prefer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think red would be the best solution, otherwise it becomes confusing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. So we'll have the red and the black at last.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So could you please make that line in red, the route that you took.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now you just told us that you never went out, but I believe that at least on occasions you did go out. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's not what the witness has said. If one goes back to the original wording of the question asked of this witness as to whether he could see the front lines, I think that it was very open to the interpretation that the witness was being asked whether he could see the front lines from where he lived. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's my recollection that he said that he didn't see them because he never went out, so that from the place where he lived. That's at least how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I could direct you, Mr. President, to the relevant line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It's page 12, line 12. That's where he was first asked. Now, witness, in this area were you able to see, since you told us that you lived in the centre of the area? And the witness replied that he couldn't. And my friend then added the interpretation that that meant that he never from where he lived or anywhere else saw the front line. That was an interpretation not available to my friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be possible, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to rephrase the question and perhaps proceed to the point you'd like to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was going straight for the aim in French, but I'm going to go more directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you lived in the area in question, and you did go out obviously on the day of the incident. In fact, you went out at least twice. And you went, you saw the front line, and you actually crossed it. I'm talking about your own drawing, your lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't see any crossing, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I can imagine that from the lines drawn that you could say that at least in a close parallel, but I do not see any crossing as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, okay, parallelly, very well, Mr. President. Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It is the same -- the question remains, Witness. I can see that on the basis of your own drawing, you went out of the area where you lived, and then the line that you mentioned, the route, was very close to the demarcation, confrontation line. Now, you did not see a single line of confrontation. Is that so? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you for your answer. You indicated in a red line the direction in regards to the opposite of Nedzarici and which stops at a certain point. Could you tell us about this location? Could you give us the precise location of this?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Which red line?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, I only see one which goes from the area of Nedzarici, which is the lateral area on the right, and it goes to the Bulevar, goes to the right, and then suddenly stops.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, I stopped there. I meant this is where we entered the settlement with this red line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So Witness, could you go to the exact location where you were going to deliver the goods.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. For the transcript, the witness added a line further on slightly to the left which stops in the centre of the enclave that he had marked. Now, Witness, this is here where the premises of the Civil Defence were. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, these were the premises of the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for this answer. Now, in relation to the area that we're interested in, that is the area that you yourself had circled, could you perhaps tell us if the buildings that are there are mostly apartment blocks, high rises or perhaps lower type of houses?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: About all of them had about eight floors, that is, ground floor and another seven floors. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in the area which is in the lower part of the area that you've marked, that is the area which is on the left-hand side of this outline, isn't it true that the houses or the buildings were a lot lower in height?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: The houses where I lived -- that I lived in, there were ground-floor houses and seven floors. And here over towards the intersection there was nothing else except the student residence. This was all destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, could you please take the pointer and then point it to the -- put it on the map and show us again. You can put the pointer -- can you indicate the area? Go to the left, please, with the pointer. No, this is going up. Go down to your left, please. A little further. Yes. Go on, please. Go on. Yes, here, in this area. You can stop, thank you. In this area here, isn't it true to say that the buildings were a lot lower in height?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How many floors approximately did the buildings in this area have? In the area you have just indicated, which is the roughly the upper left corner --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the precision of the transcript, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness was indicating a street left of the word "Nedzarici," a bit up with the names of the streets Aleja Bosne Srebrene and below it, Asima Bekmeda [phoen]. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So Witness, the question was how many floors were there in that particular area that we are calling the lower area of Nedzarici in general?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: You mean exactly where the pointer is? Or you mean this area here, up there?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, I was thinking about the area that you indicated with the pointer and where as the President just reminded you. Is the lower part -- go down. Go down. No, this is too far. This area here that you've indicated, which is roughly on the same height as the word "Nedzarici" but a little to the left. Isn't it true that in this area, the buildings were of relatively low height?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: There were no buildings; there are just family houses there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to ask you. Thank you for your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: The only building which is there is the faculty of the theology, this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Thank you. Did you see any trenches, Witness?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You have never seen trenches throughout the conflict?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, on TV, when there was electricity.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very last question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The map, Witness, that you see before you, does it correspond to what is now real, what the situation is now?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is there on this map certain details that do not correspond to the situation in the city today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you want to point at the whole map or just this part, then I had the same thing in my mind. We discussed only a very small part of the map so would you please indicate which specific part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, Mr. President. I am talking, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am talking about what you've indicated. And in the same area that you have circled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, the question is whether the part of the map we have been speaking about, whether in reality nowadays anything has changed compared to what is on this map, to your knowledge. Is there anything different now compared to what you see on the map?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: This place now looks completely different because if you'll allow me, because during the war, in this area here, this area here, there used to be houses but they were destroyed so you couldn't see anything there. And also in all these other parts of Nedzarici, new buildings have been erected. But there are also family houses. Maybe they have one or two floors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. One of the last questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, does the area that you have circled in a dotted line, does it correspond to what you called Vojnicko Polje?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. And below this area, as far as you know, there were no trenches there, were there?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: In which direction lower down below?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am talking about the map, the same area to the left below the area that you have marked in a dotted line, slightly to the left. Can go out. Go a little lower. Lower. That's above. Below. You can go down to the left. Down, down, down, please. Yes, in this area. You can stop your pointer. Thank you. Isn't it true to say slightly below that that there were trenches?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And these houses, what type of houses were they at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: In which area?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm talking about the part of that we have just indicated with the pointer. There were certain apartment blocks, certain blocks, and then below Nedzarici, go down, go down. Go down. Go down. You can follow the straight line. You have a line. You can follow the line, the vertical line. Witness, you can stop here. Yes, a little bit further, please. Go below the pointer. All this area, what kind of houses were there? Slightly to your right. What kind of buildings were they? So a little bit to your right, please. Yes, that is the left. Go to the right. Yes. Yes. You are now in that area. This entire area, I can see a number 120 in the middle. What kind of houses were in this area at the time?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, these were only family houses on this side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it took you approximately one minute to get the witness to the area where he already testified that these were family homes five minutes ago. I don't know whether there's any reason for this repetitious questioning. Please indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I wanted to be absolutely precise and correct. Thank you, Mr. President. I'm just going to confer with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am just asking a few moments from the Chamber, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this will be the very last question, Mr. President. And then we're finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'm quite willing to accept that on line 66 -- page 66, 3, you said very last question, Mr. President. And that was approximately eight minutes ago. So I keep you to the very last question, because you later indicated one of the last questions. That was a couple of minutes afterwards now. It's your very last question you do understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As I said, this will be my very last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you indicated that the houses we were trying to determine the location of. These houses had been destroyed. Now, could you tell us how they were destroyed and following what?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: In which part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we are talking --

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Which part of the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The family houses you just indicated and an area I described as the Aleja Bosne Srebrene. To your left. Where your left ring finger is approximately. The family houses there, were these destroyed?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These were not destroyed. Where were any destroyed structures? Could you please indicate, because you told us that the area had considerably changed. Could you please -- and you talked about the destruction of houses or buildings. Could you indicate where these buildings were that were destroyed?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: All of the buildings in front of the blind institute, and the institute for children were destroyed. They were no longer there. And where I'm showing now, these were family houses that were not destroyed. This part here. And all the others, below the institute for blind children, the Branka Bujica Street which is going the direction of where I was wounded, there was nothing there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, the witness was indicating the area which has the name Olsobodenje Studentski Dom, Zavod Za Slijepe and Dom Penzionera. Has is this clarified the issue you wanted to raise, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, absolutely. And as I said, this was my last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any need to re-examine the witness, Mr. Ierace? If so, I would first like to have the break. If not, I would turn to my colleagues and see whether there are any additional questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I do propose to ask some questions in re-examination, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break now until 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please bring in the witness. I do understand a message was sent to me during the break that Mr. Piletta-Zanin would like to have the year of the map, and then I think he means the black and white big map. Would it be possible for the Prosecution who tendered this map. Please be seated. Just one moment, Mr. Kadric. You don't have to sort it out now right away, unless there's any necessity now. Mr. Piletta-Zanin will then also provide us with the date of his map, because he.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's up to you, Mr. Ierace, to re-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If you wish, I could give that information now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it's not relevant at this moment, let's just wait until after the examination of the witness has been concluded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you have been asked a number of questions about your observations during the war. After you were discharged from hospital in Sarajevo, how long was it before you then went to the United Arab Emirates?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: About four or five months.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked questions also about who employed your father at the time you were shot. Who employed your father before you were shot, that is, in the period between when the conflict commenced and when you were shot?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During cross-examination, you said that there was a 2 tonne cistern fitted to your father's truck. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did the cistern contain?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: It was a plastic tank carrying water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that on the day you were shot, your father was carrying flour. Was there anything in the cistern that you remember?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: The day before, that cistern had been taken off that vehicle. A Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said also in relation to the carrying of the cistern, you went to the brewery or your father went to the brewery. As you understood it, why did you go to the brewery, that is, why did your father take the truck with the cistern to the brewery?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: To load water, because at that time we had no water supply.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked in cross-examination whether on the route you took when you were shot you could see the -- a single line of confrontation. On the route you were on when you were shot, could you see the other side of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I couldn't see the trenches. I could see this building, this institute for blind and retarded children that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I'd like to continue, because there are two new elements which have now emerged. The first concerns the cistern, and the second, the answer of the witness right now, the last question, the answer to the last question of the Prosecution because he spontaneously said, "I could not see the trenches," and he was not asked the question. And when I asked him about the trenches, he said that he knew nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although you could wonder, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether the cistern is anything new brought up, we'll allow you some questions. But let's take it seriously that you do it efficiently and quick.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as always, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the cistern that you mentioned, did it have to do anything with a cistern called Voma, I repeat Voma.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You mentioned cisterns. Does it have anything to do with a cistern called Voma?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: To begin with, I don't know what Voma means. I'll explain. This cistern which was there, it is a plastic tank which would be put inside the refrigerating tank, and he put the -- a day before we went to get the flour, it was taken out so that flour could be loaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. And my second question is you said that you could not see the trenches but does that mean that you knew where they were because you said you could not see them. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know where they were. I know that the institute for blind and retarded children, that there were front lines there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But it is true that they were trenches, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether there were any trenches. I know that the front line was there, and that from this place here, I could see the institute for blind children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I remind you that a moment ago you said that you could not see the trenches; therefore, you were aware that there were trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it's even this question that I'll not allow. It's certainly possible that you say that you didn't see something you would expect normally at a certain place, even if you don't know for sure whether they are there. If, for example, in a football stadium you say I didn't see the players, that doesn't necessarily mean that the players were there. But what you usually would expect in a football stadium is players. Sometimes they are there and sometimes they are not there. So the question suggests something which could mislead the witness. Then, is there any question of my colleagues? Judge Nieto-Navia will put questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes. How close or how far was your house from the Civil Defence headquarters or place?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: About 50, maybe 60 metres. That was the distance between my house and the Civil Defence headquarters. Yes, it was very close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If I understand you, Witness, you were sitting next to your father at the time when the incident happened. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: There was a free seat between us, between my father and me, and nobody was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's right. Yes. But that is a vehicle with the steering wheel on the left-hand side, and you were on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you said that you were hit in your right side.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in your view, this bullet which struck you came from where, from which area?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: From the direction of the institute for blind children. That is, the bullet came from there. And you can see it clearly on this map here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But on your way, you left your house?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were going back?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you were going back home.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Having delivered whatever you had to deliver.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: No, we were coming back towards the Civil Defence with the goods at the moment when it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a last question to you: You told us that when the incident took place, your father was working for the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... by Mr. Ierace, you told us that your father was in the army before the incident. The question was: "Who employed your father before you were shot, that is, in between when the conflict commenced and when you were shot?" Your answer then was: "The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us when he left the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and when he started working for the Civil Defence? Was that immediately before the incident or a considerable time before?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: My father was a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but he was also often engaged by the Civil Defence. I mean, because there were no other means of transportation, no other vehicles to carry water, then he would be taken on by the Civil Defence to collect this water and bring it so that it could be distributed to the citizens. And that day, he was working for the Civil Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you say actually is that your father was a member of the army, but at the day of the incident, he was then, upon the request of the Civil Defence, transporting flour in this case?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did I understand well that the truck of your father was never used for military purposes on those days when he was working for the army?

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: He never used that truck to do any service for the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But he did use it for the Civil Defence purposes.

utterances.speaker: FARUK KADRIC
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. Mr. Kadric, you've answered all the questions put by the parties to you, and also the additional questions the Bench had. We're fully aware that it's quite a trip for you to come from Sarajevo to The Hague, and I hope you do understand how important it is for this Court to get answers from those who have been present during those days in that area, because we need answers on questions put to you by both parties in order to prepare the decisions we'll have to take. Thank you very much in coming and helping us to fulfill this task, and a good trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please lead Mr. Kadric out of the courtroom. I didn't ask the usher to bring in the next witness, but I hope he understands what he is expected to do. We still have to deal with the exhibits. Madam Registrar, could you perhaps guide us through the paperwork. I think what we've got -- I've got no videos, no 360-degrees at this moment. I think we first have the -- yes. That's the medical report P1781, and the same number with a .1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are admitted into evidence. Then, Madam Registrar, I think we have the photos.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The x-rays.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Then we have Exhibit 1701.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which is the series of three exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have the map, P3644 FK1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I was going to say and the last exhibit is the Defence map, which is D47.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are all admitted into evidence. And when I said, "Which is the series of three exhibits," I meant to say that it was the series of three x-ray photographs. Please, Mr. Usher, would you bring in the next witness in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is merely to say that in the transcript, the date of the map that we re using is 1998, and that was not included in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay, then that has been corrected as well. Mr. Kadric, can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving testimony in this courtroom -- and let me first say welcome in this courtroom. Before giving testimony, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn statement -- solemn declaration. The text of this declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. And may I invite you to make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Mr. Kadric. Mr. Kadric, the order in this courtroom is that you'll first be examined by counsel for the Prosecution. You'll then be examined by counsel for the Defence, and if there are any questions, either during this examination or at the end by the Bench, we'll put questions to you as well. Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, would you please tell the Judge, and for the record, your name.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Fajko Kadric.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: During the conflict in Sarajevo, were you living in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: No; at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sorry. When did you move from Pale?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: On the 3rd or 4th of July, 1992. They moved us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thereafter, did you live in Sarajevo, that is, from July 1992?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before the armed conflict commenced, what was your occupation?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: I had a butcher's shop in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have that business with a relative, in particular, your brother?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: No, no, no. It was my brother-in-law. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. When did you start that business? When did you join that business?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that business, did you have a truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the size of the truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: It was for cattle -- no, rather, we had two trucks and a refrigerator truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. After the move to Sarajevo, at some point after that, did you join the army?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was that ultimately known as the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you do that?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: I believe it was the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were the forces known as at that stage that you joined, if anything?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Something like TO, I mean the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At some stage after that, did you do any tasks for an organisation known as Civilian Defence?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak up, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kadric, could you come a bit closer to the microphones, because those who are interpreting have difficulties in hearing you. So if perhaps you would move your chair a bit closer to the table and perhaps put the microphones a bit closer to you. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you first start to do tasks for Civilian Defence?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, we went to fetch water.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you first do that for Civilian Defence?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact date, but it was a daily chore. I mean whenever there would be no water, then we would go to get it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Did you start doing that at some stage in the year 1992 or after then?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: 1992, autumn of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you use to collect water -- to carry water, I should say?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: We had this refrigerated truck for meat, and we fitted in a 3-tonne cistern, and that is how we worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did you get that truck from?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: We used to carry meat beforehand it in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was it one of the vehicles that your brother-in-law had in your butchers business?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how long was the truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, 320, the cabin, and then 2 metres, maybe less. So about 5 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And was the cabin separate from the refrigerated back or was it part of the same body?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many seats were in the cabin?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: One plus two.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the -- withdraw that. Was the refrigerated part higher or lower than the cabin or the same height?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: The refrigerator was higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the height of the refrigerated back from the ground level approximately?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: About 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And how much higher was the back compared to the cabin?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: About 50 centimetres, half a metre. Perhaps more, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts were you living when you moved to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: In the Vojnicko Polje locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there an occasion when your son was travelling with you in the truck, and he was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: It was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the date that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: The 4th October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On that occasion, were you carrying anything in the truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, flour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From where had you collected the flour?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: At the bakery.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were you taking the flour?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: To the locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts in -- withdraw that. I take it you mean the locality where you lived. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Whereabouts were you when your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Well, on the street, the 10th Transversal, and where Branka Bujica Street forks off.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you make a statement to a investigator from the Tribunal on the 13th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At that time, were you shown a map of that area, and did you place some marks on that map?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you place your signature on the map?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3108.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise your signature on the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Above your signature or at least in the same area, I think there is the date of the 13th of October, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you know who placed that date there?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And I think the date at the top in the box is the 13th of November, 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, on this map, did you mark the route that you were taking immediately before your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that route -- withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the map be placed on the ELMO, in particular the part of the map which has some markings on it. That's the left hand half of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes. I went from Sarajevo, and then I went up to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. With the pointer, you are following the arrows indicating a left-hand turn, and then across at an intersection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps that question doesn't need a reply, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: We went from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, could you indicate where it was that your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think a cross appears on the map at that point. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, will you please tell the Trial Chamber what happened after you turned left and proceeded towards where we see a cross.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: When we arrived to the intersection, there was a bang, an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Whereabouts was your son at the time of the bang?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, on the right-hand side of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you said there were two seats, three seats all together, and two seats -- please wait for the question. Two seats to your right. Was he seated in the middle seat or the far right seat next to the door?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the end, right by the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. What happened after you hear the bang and the explosion?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Faruk fell on the middle seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you notice any blood?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I covered it with my hand, and I continued to drive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What part of his body did you cover?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: The neck, like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates the right side of the neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: We went about a hundred metres behind a building, and then we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you receive some assistance from some other people?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, UNPROFOR was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did they -- withdraw that. Was your son then taken from that area to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Following his discharge from hospital, was he ultimately sent to the United Arab Emirates for further medical treatment?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did he remain there for approximately 19 months?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: He left in February, and he returned in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did he leave in February 1994?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: In 199 -- yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. What were you wearing on that day in particular at the time that your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: I had a coat on. I had a civilian coat and trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you wearing anything to do with the military?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: No, no, we didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was your son wearing?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: He had jeans on, and on top, I don't know what he had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What colour was the truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: The cabin was blue, and the body was white.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any writing on the right-hand side of the truck as you faced towards the front of the truck in the direction you were driving?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, it said Mesnica, "butchers" in large letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the weather like at the time your son was shot?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Fair weather.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What time was it approximately?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Quarter past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the window, that is the window of the cabin nearest your son, open or closed?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Later, did you inspect your truck for damage?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: The truck was hit on the right-hand side at the door, the frame of the door at the height of the neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness be shown Exhibit P3107.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the map might stay at the witness's desk. I'll be coming back to that shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the piece of paper in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that a drawing that you did at the time that you made your statement dated the 13th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it bear your signature?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, might that be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Is that a drawing by you of your truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does it show the side that was closest to your son?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On that drawing, would you please indicate what damage was caused during this incident, if any?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: This was the entry point of the bullet here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please take a blue marker and draw an arrow to that point of damage.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell us where that point was? In other words, was it on the frame of the cabin, on the door, on the frame of the door, or where?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes, the frame. On the frame of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, were you able to determine the direction from which the bullet had come?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How were you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: The entry point is exactly the size of a bullet, and then it fragmented and hit my son there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you able to tell the direction the bullet had come from, that is, before it hit your truck?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. How were you able to determine that?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: On the front -- on the dashboard of the car, the bullet had cut it, and it went on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, going back to the map, you placed a cross to indicate where you were when your son was shot. That cross is on an intersection. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How fast were you travelling at the time your son was shot approximately?

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
utterances.text: About 20 or 30 kilometres per hour because we were loaded with a full load, and it was going uphill.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to the position of the vehicle when your son was shot and the damage on the dashboard and the entry point hole on the side, that is the right-hand side of your vehicle, were you able to conclude firstly from which side of the vehicle the shot had come? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FAJKO KADRIC
